newsitem.title: UK: London stocks edge higher, Tokyo ends losing streak.
newsitem.headline: London stocks edge higher, Tokyo ends losing streak.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Renewed takeover interest in the regional electricity companies provided much of the interest in an otherwise subdued start to the week in London, traders said. A bid from the United States by CalEnergy unit, CE Electric for Northern Electric took many in the market by surprise and helped lift prices across the board initially. However, shares failed to make much headway and a lack of news on other fronts left them drifting for much of the session.
The FTSE 100 ended the day just 2.9 points higher at 4,025.3, with gainers leading losers 55 to 38.

FRANKFURT- German shares got the week off to a solid start as the firm dollar and a stream of positive corporate news helped ease the tension which sparked sharp market declines last week. Heavyweight blue chip companies including Daimler-Benz and BASF led an advance which added more than one percent to the 30-share DAX index. The DAX ended floor dealings up 29.61 points at 2,703.83. In post-bourse trade the index rose 12.54 to 2,703.33.

PARIS - French shares closed easier in consolidation from recent highs and on caution about a series of U.S. data including inflation, economic growth and unemployment, as well as the pending presidential elections. A higher start on Wall Street lifted shares from the day's lows in moderate volume during a French school holiday week. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 12.04 points at 2,150.39.

ZURICH - Swiss shares gave up some of their early gains in the second half of the session but closed slightly higher after a friendly Wall Street opening gave them a late boost. Dealers hoped U.S. economic data due this week would add pep to slow trading, but investors were likely to remain cautious as U.S. presidential elections draw closer. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 2.07 points to 2,415.26 points.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks snapped out of their five-day losing streak, ending on a positive tone. Turnover was extremely thin as most investors were on the sidelines, searching for sound reasons to trade on. The 225-issue Nikkei average was 145.44 points or 0.70 percent higher at 20,885.41. Its December futures added 200 points to settle at 20,970.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower, hit by an afternoon slide in prices as a pause in the market's recent rally prompted investors to take profits. The Hang Seng closed 125.61 points lower at 12,262.77.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed slightly weaker after a bout of selling in the resources sector in the last hour of trading. The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 1.1 points lower at 2,334.1, well off its intra-day high of 2,346.9.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares ended weak in busy trading, battered by an ailing rand. Gold shares finished firm lifted by a better rand gold price and stronger bullion. Comments from central Reserve Bank governer Chris Stals' that he did not see an interest rate cut next year, but possibly a rate hike, added to the gloom on the market. The overall index shed 20.9 points to 6,964.3, the industrial index was off 37.5 points to 8,221.4 and the gold index gained 13.8 points to 1,717.7.
